title: Identification and validation of hub genes for kidney renal clear cell carcinoma treated with metformin and everolimus combination therapy.
authors: He, Shenbao; Zhang, Bin; Zhang, Lili; Shang, Panfeng; Yue, Zhongjin
one_liner_zh: 该文通过转录组测序和分子对接研究二甲双胍与依维莫司联合治疗肾透明细胞癌的核心基因及转录因子调控，虽涉及TF-DNA结合预测，但核心是药物靶点筛选而非TF-DNA互作机制建模，方法以实验和常规生信为主，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a prevalent malignancy of the urinary system that presents significant health and economic burdens. Despite existing treatments such as surgery and targeted therapies, challenges remain due to suboptimal efficacy and high recurrence rates. Previous studies have indicated that metformin and everolimus individually exhibit inhibitory effects on RCC. However, their synergistic potential when combined has not been fully elucidated. Therefore, this paper identified the antiproliferative effect and the hub genes that undergo significant changes in 786-O cells when treated with the combination drugs and their underlying mechanisms to inform the search for kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) therapeutic targets. METHODS: The effects of the combination of metformin and everolimus on 786-O cells viability, migration and invasion were investigated. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) among different drug treatment groups were identified through ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing, raw data processing and differential expression analysis. The target genes were obtained by taking the intersection of different DEGs, and hub genes were identified by Maximal Clique Centrality (MCC) and Molecular Complex Detection (MCODE) algorithms, expression validation, and Kaplan-Meier (K-M) survival curve plotting. Subsequently, transcription factors (TFs) regulating the hub genes were identified and drug-hub gene interactions were explored through molecular docking. In addition, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) demonstrated hub gene-related biological functions and pathways, and gene set variation analysis (GSVA) explored differential pathways between different drug treatment groups. Finally, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was performed to verify the expression difference of hub genes among four groups. RESULTS: The combination of metformin and everolimus is more effective than monotherapy at inhibiting cell viability, migration, and invasion in 786-O cells. In total, 3,030 DEG1, 2,953 DEG2, 3,591 DEG3, 1,571 DEG4 and 4,064 DEG5 were identified, yielding five target genes. After MCC and MCODE algorithms, expression validation, and K-M survival curve plotting, target genes were all noted as hub genes (SPC25, NCAPH, MCM10, UHRF1, SMC4). Eleven TFs regulated more than two hub genes, and the binding energy of metformin with SPC25 and everolimus with SMC4 was the lowest. Hub genes were negatively correlated with lysosome and positively associated with cell cycle, and the P13K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway was significantly positively correlated with hub genes. CONCLUSIONS: Metformin and everolimus are synergistic in anticancer effects on RCC. Based on transcriptomic data, this study obtained five hub genes associated with everolimus and metformin combination therapy in KIRC to inform KIRC-related research.
abstract_zh: 背景：肾细胞癌（RCC）是泌尿系统常见的恶性肿瘤，给健康和经济带来沉重负担。尽管已有手术和靶向治疗等现有疗法，但由于疗效欠佳和复发率高，仍面临挑战。既往研究表明，二甲双胍和依维莫司单独使用对RCC具有抑制作用。然而，两者联合使用的协同潜力尚未完全阐明。因此，本文鉴定了联合用药处理786-O细胞时的抗增殖效应及显著变化的核心基因（hub genes）及其潜在机制，以期为肾透明细胞癌（KIRC）治疗靶点的寻找提供参考。方法：研究了二甲双胍和依维莫司联合使用对786-O细胞活力、迁移和侵袭的影响。通过核糖核酸（RNA）测序、原始数据处理和差异表达分析，鉴定了不同药物处理组间的差异表达基因（DEGs）。通过取不同DEGs的交集获得靶基因，并利用最大团中心性（MCC）和分子复合物检测（MCODE）算法、表达验证及Kaplan-Meier（K-M）生存曲线绘制鉴定核心基因。随后，鉴定了调控核心基因的转录因子（TFs），并通过分子对接探索了药物-核心基因相互作用。此外，基因集富集分析（GSEA）展示了核心基因相关的生物学功能和通路，基因集变异分析（GSVA）探索了不同药物处理组间的差异通路。最后，采用实时定量聚合酶链反应（qRT-PCR）验证四组间核心基因的表达差异。结果：二甲双胍和依维莫司联合使用在抑制786-O细胞活力、迁移和侵袭方面比单药治疗更有效。共鉴定出3,030个DEG1、2,953个DEG2、3,591个DEG3、1,571个DEG4和4,064个DEG5，得到五个靶基因。经MCC和MCODE算法、表达验证及K-M生存曲线绘制后，所有靶基因均被认定为核心基因（SPC25、NCAPH、MCM10、UHRF1、SMC4）。十一个转录因子调控两个以上核心基因，且二甲双胍与SPC25、依维莫司与SMC4的结合能最低。核心基因与溶酶体呈负相关，与细胞周期呈正相关，且P13K/Akt/mTOR信号通路与核心基因显著正相关。结论：二甲双胍和依维莫司在RCC抗癌效应上具有协同作用。基于转录组数据，本研究获得了与依维莫司和二甲双胍联合治疗KIRC相关的五个核心基因，为KIRC相关研究提供参考。
